citation: Homes for George Glessner and Frances Glessner Lee, 1700-1706 S. Prairie Avenue, under construction, 1901. Photograph by George Glessner. Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'George Glessner, photographer', The Story of a House (blog), 12 January 2015.
author: George Glessner (per the blog; the caption names no photographer)
repository: Glessner House Museum blog 'The Story of a House' (the museum's George Glessner photographs, per the blog). Prairie library images a16-ghm-blog-1700-1706-construction-1901 and st-ghm-1700-1706-under-construction-1901, the same picture catalogued twice, their rights recorded there as 'pending - permission requested' (rights-requests/ghm-george-glessner-2026-10.md); the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a16-ghm-blog-1700-1706-construction-1901.jpg), committed since T-3212 at data/sources/assets/glessner_1700_1706_construction_1901_t3212/ with its attribution.
locator: The whole photograph, 675 x 494 px: 1708 Prairie at the left edge, the pair's street front from 1706's south corner to 1700's north corner (1700's front half behind a young street tree), 1638 Prairie's gable at the right edge.
rights_note: Permission for the museum's scans was requested on 2026-10-02 and is pending; the photographs are unpublished works by George Glessner (d. 1929). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-3212) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-28 (T-3212) from the image store's reference copy, 675 x 494 px greyscale (sha256 1ff92f1791176a4903d03470860b37f47871e6cca149297be8248f40c98f081b). Both library entries say the camera faced south-west; 1708 stands nearest at the left and the pair's cornice falls toward 1700, so it stood SOUTH-east of the pair looking north-west (T-3212's camera).
note: The pair in the summer of 1901, a year before the Glessner and Lee families moved in (1902): the brick shell finished to its cornice, the slate mansard and its pedimented dormers and chimneys up, every window opening still unglazed. Neither porch is built: 1706's door is a wide opening under a stone lintel with a sign board on it, and the stone string course under the principal storey's sills is already laid. Before the pair a spear railing on a stone curb runs on from 1708's to a pair of capped piers before 1706's south part and stops there (through T-3212's camera, at about 0.6-2.3 m and 2.8 m north of 1706's south corner); in the yard a builder's timber shed and sand heaps; a young tree on the parkway before 1700; overhead wires. It is evidence of 1901, not of 1904: what it shows unfinished, or not yet built, is argued in the pair's match records (data/reference_views/*/ghm_construction_1901.match.json), not copied.
what_it_supplies: the pair's street front under construction: the places and heights of its openings, its string course, cornice line and mansard
the dormers, the chimneys and the party line's downpipe in 1901
the railing and curb before 1706 in 1901, its gateway and its end, and the builder's yard
1708 Prairie's north end and 1638 Prairie's gable in 1901
what_it_does_not_supply: the porches, the balconettes and the glazing, which were not yet built
1700's north half, hidden behind the street tree
